reviewer.method: Read all 84 start/mid/end evidence PNGs for shot-14 through shot-41 with the Read tool; cross-referenced project.json layer/keyframe data and evidence.json shot timing for every shot; extracted and inspected continuous-clip frames at 6-15fps via ffmpeg for shots with suspected static holds or hard pose-swaps (shot-22, shot-28, shot-33, shot-40 laptop-close); measured whole-film loudness with ffmpeg ebur128 (peak=true) and per-shot intelligibility with ffmpeg volumedetect on 7 sampled talk/hold windows in the body; sampled pre-existing shot-0..13 frame extractions plus shot-13-end/shot-14-start to confirm the scene4/scene5 cut at 60.183s; compared craft quality against 8 Ryan V4 reference frames (ref-0.5, ref-3, ref-6 n/a, ref-9, ref-12, ref-15 n/a, ref-18, ref-20.5) in review/ref-ryan-v4/. Sound intelligibility was measured via loudness/level tools, not auditioned by ear.

observations.detail: Shot-4 (confirmed baseline) establishes the floating 'writing pencil' + character-seated-apart convention that recurs legitimately through the body (e.g. shots 16-25, 32, 36, 38); confirms this is an accepted stylistic device, not a contact fault, when it reappears later.

Shot-13 end ('Mendukung kalimat yang mana?' with a claim card and an article-finding card) hands off cleanly at 60.183s into shot-14's reading-card exercise; same notebook/card visual language carries the scene-4-to-scene-5 cut without a jarring reset.

Shot-14: red header 'pertanyaan sementara' is fused with the notebook's spiral-ring band for the whole shot, the first instance of a recurring ring-overlap typography fault in the body (recurs in shots 16, 17 and, for body text, shot-25).
Shot-22: the notebook prop annotated 'Ardipal mendorong buku ke arah Vidka' only wiggles ~60px and never travels toward Vidka; the described push is not perceptible on screen.

Shot-25: the first line of the handwritten research question is written directly across the spiral rings, the most severe instance of the ring-overlap fault since it affects two lines of body copy rather than a short header.

Shot-28: the questionnaire prop annotated 'diangkat dan dibaca' (lifted and read) only moves ~20px/0.03rad across the full 2.0s hold; the shot reads as a static image with Vidka holding her own separate paper rather than the questionnaire being lifted.

Shot-33: player-b's turn to a startled pose is a hard pose-swap rather than an eased turn, but lands cleanly on the beat ('menoleh' label, clock updates to 12:04) and is unambiguous on a single frame.
Shot-36: the card-swap from 'memahami proses' to 'menguji pengaruh' is a clean, well-composed single pivot with no overlap between the two cards.

Shot-40: the laptop-close sequence (open to closed) is correctly staged and resolves cleanly by the end of the shot, with the closed laptop sitting flush on the desk and no leftover open-laptop artwork -- initially looked like a possible double-prop fault from the start/mid crops but is confirmed resolved on frame-level inspection.

Final shot-41 hold closes the film with the same task-card/checkmark convention used at shots 21 and 31, giving a consistent, satisfying close; whole-film integrated loudness measures -20.3 LUFS with true peak -1.6 dBFS, no clipping detected across the full 182.6s runtime.

Ref-0.5 ('Write.') shows a single stick figure at a desk with a monitor, mug and plant, each object fully opaque with no overlapping outlines, and a bold hand-lettered headline plus one grey supporting line -- the craft bar this project's B1 contract is measured against.

Ref-3 ('Refresh.') reuses the same desk illustration with only the icon state changed, demonstrating disciplined asset reuse across beats, the same discipline seen in this project's repeated desk/notebook/pencil assets.

Ref-9 ('But here's what hurts.') shows a single, unmistakable physical action (a stack of videos being pushed and toppling) with motion lines on every unit -- a higher bar for legible single-prop motion than this project's shot-22/shot-28 sub-pixel wiggles meet.
No character on screen this shot (card/notebook insert only); note-card and notebook line art match the established flat-outline style seen in baseline shot-4/shot-9 inserts.
